This reproductive strategy ensures substantial per-offspring maternal investment despite a low annual fecundity.

The species' ecological role as a long-distance seed disperser in fragmented island landscapes is likely reinforced by this life-history strategy, as the extended lifespan and low reproductive rate promote population stability and resilience to environmental perturbation.
